A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Discrete Distribution Networks. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and reordered supplementary sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original DDN generation, reconstruction, ablation and latent-classification results on image datasets, together with synthetic distribution-fitting experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the quantitative tables and extensive qualitative experiments in the appendices.

M1.justification: The architecture, nearest-output training, layer-averaged L2 loss, Split-and-Prune, conditional sampling and three training techniques remain unchanged. The new equations explicitly describe existing operations; they do not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: v2 removes v1 supplementary Section 6's brief report of facial-recognition ZSCG experiments among the raw experimental results. This narrowly reduces documented task coverage; the external examples themselves are unavailable. All directly displayed datasets and tasks are retained, and the new IGN comparison uses the existing CelebA-HQ setting.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes BigGAN and Denoising Diffusion from the CIFAR-10 comparison while retaining the other five baselines. v2 Figure 7 adds an actual sample/FID comparison against the previously cited Idempotent Generative Network (IGN) on CelebA-HQ.

E3.justification: The shared experiments retain their stated training/test assignments, resolutions, model sizes, K/L values, sampling settings, FID/rFID metrics and toy-experiment procedures. The EDM implementation reference is newly disclosed information. The added IGN comparison does not document a distinct evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Table 2's component and K ablations, the MNIST Split-and-Prune/Chain Dropout study, nearest-neighbor checks, reconstruction examples and latent analyses are retained. Their relocation and renumbering do not introduce new analyses; Figure 7 adds a baseline comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the empirical comparisons. The point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Shared DDN scores are unchanged, including CIFAR-10 FID 52.0, FFHQ FID 43.1, CelebA-HQ FID 35.4 and Tables 2–3. The BigGAN 14.1 and Denoising Diffusion 3.2 entries disappear. v2 Figure 7 adds IGN FID 39 and a finding of clearer DDN details/fewer artifacts; this is a new comparison, not a v1-to-v2 DDN performance gain.

T1.justification: New Equations (1)–(5) express the already specified greedy selection, layerwise loss, latent sequence, averaged objective and classifier-guided argmax. The existing distribution-fitting reasoning and compression formulas remain; no substantive new mathematical result, assumption or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion stop presenting compression as a headline property and concentrate on general ZSCG, although compression remains in the introduction and applications. The gradient-free, non-pixel novelty assertion is brought forward from v1's supplement rather than introduced as an entirely new capability.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds the limitation that ZSCG requires L×K guidance-model evaluations, with batching as mitigation. The CIFAR discussion shifts toward task difficulty and ZSCG's relevance. Conversely, v2 removes the explicit caveat about failures in unfiltered facial-recognition and CLIP-editing results.

D1.justification: v2 identifies EDM as the implementation foundation, describes training parameters as nearly identical to EDM, and discusses code/model-weight release. It removes the supplementary-ZIP disclosure and assurance of no filtering or rejection sampling. Hardware and model specifications remain unchanged; actual resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds EDM, DDNM, Steered Diffusion and FreeDoM references and distinguishes pixel-domain conditioning from gradient-dependent guidance. It expands discussion of the already cited IGN and removes the general survey and paired/unpaired translation references. These are targeted positioning changes, beyond citation-format and publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites of the abstract, introduction, generation-quality discussion and conclusion, plus an expanded objective-function explanation. Conditional-generation positioning moves into the introduction, supplementary sections are reordered, and author/header text changes. Most methodological and experimental prose remains intact.

P2.justification: The document switches from two columns to predominantly one column, substantially resizing and relocating figures and tables. Figure 1's panels are rearranged, the IGN comparison figure is added, Table 1 loses its One-Step Generation column, and Table 2 shortens its reconstruction-column labels. Earlier result figures remain present.

improvement.justification: Explicit objectives, more precise ZSCG positioning and the guidance-cost limitation improve clarity and qualification. However, v2 removes the two strongest CIFAR-10 baseline scores and the unfiltered-failure disclosure, while the added IGN comparison lacks matched-protocol documentation. These benefits and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
